# @forgesworn/qr

> QR code encoder and decoder with no dependencies, for browsers, workers and Node. Versions 1-40, levels L/M/Q/H, numeric, alphanumeric and byte modes with optimal mixed segmentation, optional UTF-8 ECI, SVG, canvas and terminal output. The decoder reads RGBA or greyscale camera frames, including rotated, tilted, mirrored and inverted codes. Tests compare 148 symbols module for module with an independent encoder, read output back with an independent decoder, require the decoder to read at least as many synthetic distorted frames as that decoder, and hold a floor on a set of 184 real photographs, none of which may decode to the wrong text.

ESM only, Node.js 22.13+.

## Install

```bash
npm install @forgesworn/qr
```

## API

- `encode(data: string | Uint8Array, options?: EncodeOptions): QrCode` - options `ecc` ('L'|'M'|'Q'|'H', default 'M'), `version` (1-40), `minVersion`, `mask` (0-7), `mode` ('numeric'|'alphanumeric'|'byte': one segment of that mode; default: the fewest-bits mix of segments), `eci` (boolean, applies when there is a byte segment). Throws `QrCapacityError` (a RangeError) when the data does not fit; a `version` below `minVersion` throws a RangeError.
- `QrCode` - `{ version, ecc, mask, mode, segments, size, modules }`; `segments` is `{ mode, count }[]` in order and `mode` the widest of them; `modules` is a row-major Uint8Array, 1 = dark, no quiet zone.
- `isDark(qr, x, y): boolean` - false outside the symbol.
- `toSvg(qr, { margin = 4, dark = '#000', light = '#fff' | null, title? }): string`
- `drawCanvas(canvas, qr, { width = 8 px per module, margin = 4, dark, light | null }): void` - any HTMLCanvasElement or OffscreenCanvas; resizes it to width square.
- `toTerminal(qr, { margin = 4, ink = 'light' | 'dark' }): string` - half-block text; 'light' ink for dark terminal backgrounds.
- `decode(image: { data, width, height }, { rowStride?, channels?: 1 | 4, inversion?: 'normal' | 'inverted' | 'both' }): DecodeResult | undefined` - data is RGBA (ImageData) or greyscale; result `{ text, bytes, version, ecc, mask, eci, corrected, mirrored, inverted, location, structuredAppend?, fnc1? }`; `text` follows the ECI, else UTF-8, Shift_JIS or Latin-1 by content, and kanji and hanzi segments read as text; `structuredAppend` is `{ index, total, parity }`, `fnc1` is `{ position: 'first' | 'second', applicationIndicator? }`; undefined when no readable code is found.
- `decodeModules(modules, size)` - reads a row-major module grid (no quiet zone), straight or mirrored.
- The decoder is built to return `undefined` rather than a wrong text: a block corrected past the standard's capacity is refused. Work on a frame is capped, but a frame with no code costs more than one with a code, so throttle camera loops.

## Example

```ts
import { encode, toSvg } from '@forgesworn/qr'
const svg = toSvg(encode('https://example.com/', { ecc: 'Q' }))

import { decode } from '@forgesworn/qr'
const text = decode(ctx.getImageData(0, 0, w, h))?.text
```

## Common mistakes

- ESM only: `import`, never `require`.
- `decode` takes pixels (`{ data, width, height }`, RGBA or grey), not an `<img>` or `<video>`: draw to a canvas and pass `getImageData(...)`.
- `decode` and `decodeModules` return `undefined`, not `null`, when nothing reads; they throw only for arguments that cannot be a picture.
- `isDark(qr, x, y)`: column then row.
- `encode` is synchronous; `toSvg` returns a string, not an element.
- `modules` has no quiet zone: add 4 modules of margin in your own drawing.
- Options that shape the symbol (`ecc`, `version`, `mask`, `mode`) go to `encode`; options for how it looks (`margin`, `dark`, `light`, `width`, `title`) go to the renderer.
- Throttle camera loops to a few scans a second.

## Recipes and migration

The README has complete, typechecked recipes (SVG, canvas and PNG download, terminal, custom drawing, payment links, bytes, capacity errors, camera scanning, uploaded images, workers, Node, greyscale planes) and tables for migrating from `qrcode`, `qrcode-generator`, `jsQR` and camera-wrapping scanners.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/forgesworn/qr/blob/main/README.md): recipes, the full API, common mistakes and migration tables
- [SPEC](https://github.com/forgesworn/qr/blob/main/SPEC.md): exact encoder behaviour for ports, and the decoder's pipeline
- [Vectors](https://github.com/forgesworn/qr/blob/main/vectors/README.md): what a port in another language checks itself against
